newsitem.title: USA: Kaiser seeks $120 mln pretax net improvement.
newsitem.headline: Kaiser seeks $120 mln pretax net improvement.

text.p: Kaiser Aluminum Corp chief executive George Haymaker told shareholders at the company's annual meeting Thursday that Kaiser is looking to improve pretax profits on its existing businesses by $120 million.
The company reported earnings of $8.2 million, or less than a penny a share, on revenues of $2.2 billion in 1996.

Haymaker said "We intend to improve the profitability of our existing businesses by at least $120 million per year pre-tax, equal to about $1.00 per share, relative to 1996 performance, with the full effect felt during 1998."
He added that the company would work to accomplish this goal by reducing costs, improving product mix, and increasing throughput and productivity.

Haymaker said that of the the $120 million, $72 million would come from Kaiser Aluminum Commodities, primarily from lower costs, with a smaller contribution from increased output. About $21 million would come from Flat Rolled Products through increased productivity and improvements in product mix at the Trentwood, Wash., rolling mill, and about $16 million would come from Engineered Products, primarily in raw materials costs, process improvements, efficiencies and productivity.
The remaining $11 million would come through a reduction in corporate overhead expenses.

Haymaker also said that the company has an equity shelf registration statement on file, and "We anticipate that at some point, when the markets are right, we will bring additional equity into the company -- probably in connection with one or another of our earnings growth initiatives." But he noted that the company has no present plans to offer equity securities.
